target: UTM-bundled QEMU/HVF, AArch64 PCI graphical guest, one vCPU, VirtIO keyboard/tablet, WAV-backed virtio-sound-pci
command: QEMU=build/utm-qemu-probe/qemu-probe QEMU_VIRT='-L /Applications/UTM.app/Contents/Resources/qemu -machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 1 -m 1024 -device virtio-ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -audiodev wav,id=sound0,path=build/psalmody-current-c161.wav -device virtio-sound-pci,audiodev=sound0' ZEAL_COMPAT_LOG_PATH=build/check-psalmody-current-c161-2026-11-12.log python3 -u scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-psalmody --probe-psalmody-audio-timer
verified: Psalmody launched through the graphical terminal, accepted note input, generated playback, exited with Shift+Escape, and returned to a terminal that evaluated 40+2 as 42.
The experimental QEMU audio timer delivered 24 IRQs during the app run.
The WAV-backed VirtIO sound device captured stereo 16-bit PCM at 44,100 Hz for 0.4 seconds: 28,224 of 35,280 samples nonzero, peak amplitude 7,000, RMS 6,215.35, dominant tone about 520 Hz.
